questions.q: Why are people called a resource, and what factors affect the distribution of population?
answer: People are called human resources because their skills, abilities and knowledge allow them to use all other resources and create wealth, making them the most valuable resource of all.

answer.text: Population is very unevenly spread over the Earth: roughly ninety per cent of people live on about ten per cent of the land. Population density, the number of people per square kilometre, is high in South and East Asia, Europe and north-eastern USA, and low in deserts, high mountains, dense forests and polar regions.
Distribution is influenced by physical factors such as topography, climate, soil, and the availability of water and minerals, and by human factors such as industries, transport and job opportunities.

questions.q: Explain how population changes, and what a population pyramid shows.

answer.text: The population of a place changes because of births, deaths and migration. The natural growth rate is the birth rate minus the death rate. Migration adds people through immigration, when they move in, and reduces them through emigration, when they move out; rural-to-urban migration leads to urbanisation.

A population pyramid, or age-sex pyramid, shows the number of males and females in each age group. A broad-based pyramid means there are many children and a high birth rate, while a narrow-based one indicates an ageing population.
